Sad to think that so many American made classics have been reduced to cheap knockoffs or ridiculously overpriced recreations. Quality was never cheap but it was affordable and lasting 50+ years ago.

Honestly... I'm hesitant to spend a lot on wallets etc., but I'm kind of in love with the iron snail wallet. Looks amazing. I LOVE the small pocket on the outside, it's like a quick access to slip in a single card. Would be useful for my public trans. ticket. Also seems like a great size. Solid balance between space and form factor (compact). It did look a little thick when you showed the new one but I'm sure it just looks that way of will flatten down and soften over time. 

On silly thing to ask is if there's space for coins and cash? Sure, bills ofc, but I'm based in Europe and we still rely a lot on cash and especially coins in most places. Really makes it difficult to find the right wallet when you're expecting to carry some coins eventually.

But fantastic work with all your products, I'm so happy to see your vision finally manifest. Must be an incredible feeling to hold those first prototypes and see them develop over months and months. Congratulations?

The wallet is my favourite so far but I also adore the messenger back, the second version you showed. The number lock is such a fun idea and adds a little quirk to the already gorgeous bag! It gives me some steampunk vibes for no reason at all haha.

To be honest, I'm usually avoiding leather products as a vegan. It's really difficult. I just love to see the patina, the daily use and the wear and tear develop on them. I've avoided leather products for the longest time but eventually changed my mind. I still try to avoid them most of the time... But honestly? Leather is a beautiful material. It feels so... I can't put a finger on it but there's some sense of connection to see the imprint you and your life have on an object and how you're actively shaping it. Giving it meaning and seeing the marks physically. And a sense of comfort you rarely get with most materials nowadays. It has some warmth... Some comfort .. maybe I'm just holding my phone too much but those... "Organic materials",  especially when we're talking paper or ink or paint etc... there's a spark there.

Another reason I slowly start getting leather products again is just pure durability. 
Boots made from vegan leather? Bro.. that's plastic. Let's call it what it is. It's not durable. It's shit in a lot of ways (great on some others) but I just feel like it's a horrible leather replacement. After a couple of years they are probably broken or not usable anymore and when you throw them away (which I don't but whatever) they rot in some ditch for hundreds of years. Probably thousands. That's horrible.... So I try to strike a balance somehow... I'm vegan not only because I love animals but also because it's just more sustainable. And vegan leather is the opposite of sustainable.

Leather products will probably deteriorate after a while, but the incredible thing about leather is YOU PROBABLY WON'T HAVE TO THROW IT AWAY ANYWAY. If you care for it. Seriously. My dad has a pair of doc martens from when he was in England, back when they were a seriously well-made product. He has like 5-7 pairs of them. Pretty sure except one new pair he got a few years ago, they're all 30+ years old. A few probably over forty? 
To be fair! The oldest ones quite literally fall apart. Got holes in them etc. Wouldn't wear them as fashion choices or as a regular daily shoe. But he STILL WEARS THEM. He uses the oldest ones as work boots when he's working in the garden. Man they look like shit, all worn through etc. it's beautiful. 

My apologies for the lengthy comment, just felt like sharing that little story.
